Bring your own data: building an exploreDE file

Source: vignettes/bring-your-own-data.Rmd
bring-your-own-data.Rmd

exploreDE reads one file format: an .h5ad (AnnData) file in the exploreDE/1.0 layout. In R, build_explore_h5ad() writes it for you, whatever pipeline produced your data. This vignette covers:

  1. installing exploreDE and running it on your own machine;
  2. building a file, from counts only up to counts + DE + pathways;
  3. checking the file before you open it;
  4. what to do when your column names aren’t recognised;
  5. organisms without an annotation package (your own GO terms and enrichment);
  6. writing the file from outside R, and saving your settings in the app.

Every example below runs as written against the two datasets that ship with the package (inst/examples/).

Install and run 

install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("fgcz/exploreDE")   # pulls in the Bioconductor dependencies

Start the app with:

library(exploreDE)
exploreDE("my_data.h5ad")   # open straight into your file
exploreDE()                 # or start on the landing page

On the landing page, use Choose exploreDE .h5ad file(s) to upload your file (up to 1 GB per upload), or load the demo dataset. The file is read into memory for your session only. The menu then shows only the tabs your data supports: DE tabs need a DE table, and pathway tabs need pathway results. To compare contrasts across files, upload several at once: the first opens in the tabs, and the contrasts of all of them are loaded into the Multi DE tabs, where Data Selection can add more files later.

What goes into a file

Only three things are required:

Argument What it is
x the counts: a matrix (features × samples), a named list of matrices (e.g. list(counts = , normalised = )), or a DESeqDataSet
coldata sample metadata, one row per sample, rownames = the counts’ column names
omics "rnaseq", "proteomics", or "crispr"

Everything else is optional: rowdata (feature annotation), de (one DE table per contrast), pathways (ORA/GSEA results per contrast), plus labels such as organism, ref_build, and factors.

library(exploreDE)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
out_dir <- tempdir()

Counts only

The shipped RNA-seq example is a SUSHI/DESeq2 result. Using only its counts and sample table gives the smallest valid file:

se <- readRDS(system.file("examples/genomics/deResult.rds", package = "exploreDE"))

build_explore_h5ad(
  assay(se, "counts"),
  out     = file.path(out_dir, "counts_only.h5ad"),
  omics   = "rnaseq",
  coldata = colData(se)
)

Proteomics with one contrast

The shipped proteomics example is a prolfqua result. Its DE table sits in rowData as a nested table, with prolfqua’s own column names (diff, p.value, FDR). You pass it as it is; the column dictionary (below) recognises those names.

se_prot <- readRDS(system.file("examples/proteomics/SummarizedExperiment.rds",
                               package = "exploreDE"))
de_prot <- as.data.frame(rowData(se_prot)$constrast_B_vs_A)

build_explore_h5ad(
  x       = list(raw = assay(se_prot, "rawData"),
                 transformed = assay(se_prot, "transformedData")),
  out     = file.path(out_dir, "proteomics.h5ad"),
  omics   = "proteomics",
  coldata = colData(se_prot),
  rowdata = de_prot,
  factors = "G_",
  de      = list(B_vs_A = de_prot)
)

RNA-seq with DE and pathways

The same SUSHI result, this time with everything: two count layers, feature annotation, the DE statistics (SUSHI keeps them in rowData) and the clusterProfiler ORA and GSEA results from its metadata.

build_explore_h5ad(
  x         = list(counts = assay(se, "counts"), normalised = assay(se, "xNorm")),
  out       = file.path(out_dir, "rnaseq_full.h5ad"),
  omics     = "rnaseq",
  organism  = "Homo sapiens",
  ref_build = metadata(se)$param$refBuild,
  coldata   = colData(se),
  rowdata   = rowData(se),
  factors   = "Condition [Factor]",
  de        = list(diff_vs_undiff = rowData(se)),
  pathways  = list(diff_vs_undiff = list(ora  = metadata(se)$enrichResult,
                                          gsea = metadata(se)$enrichResultGSEA))
)

de and pathways are named by contrast; add one entry per contrast. Name a contrast <test>_vs_<reference>, where both groups are levels of one coldata factor (diff_vs_undiff above); other names are an error.

Pathway results can be clusterProfiler objects (enrichResult, gseaResult), plain data.frames, or nested lists of either (as above: BP/MF/CC × up/down/both). A plain data.frame must use clusterProfiler’s column names: ID, Description, p.adjust, GeneRatio, Count, geneID for ORA, plus enrichmentScore, NES, setSize, core_enrichment for GSEA. clusterProfiler objects are filtered to p.adjust <= enrichment_padj_max (default 0.1); data.frames are stored as given. With clusterProfiler objects, the network, ridge and running-score plots are available too; with data.frames, the table-based pathway plots are.

Check the file before you open it 

eds <- new_explore_dataset(file.path(out_dir, "rnaseq_full.h5ad"))
eds
#> <ExploreDatasetH5AD  (h5ad)>
#>   data_type:        RNASeq
#>   feature_id_kind:  gene
#>   organism:         Homo sapiens
#>   ref_build:        Homo_sapiens/GENCODE/GRCh38.p13/Annotation/Release_42-2023-01-30
#>   samples x features: 9 x 21057
#>   factors (1):
#>     condition  (primary): diff, undiff
#>   contrasts (1): diff_vs_undiff
#>   primary_contrast: diff_vs_undiff
#>   assays:           counts, normalised, normalised_log2, vst, tpm, fpkm
#>   enrichment:       ora, gsea

eds$has_de()                                   # TRUE: a DE table was supplied
#> [1] TRUE
eds$has_pvalue()                               # TRUE only if a raw p-value was found
#> [1] TRUE
d <- eds$de(eds$primary_contrast())
c(log2fc_missing = all(is.na(d$effect_log2fc)),
  fdr_missing    = all(is.na(d$score_fdr)))   # both should be FALSE
#> log2fc_missing    fdr_missing 
#>          FALSE          FALSE

If a DE column wasn’t recognised it comes through as NA rather than as an error, so do this check before trusting the file.

How columns are recognised

You don’t tell build_explore_h5ad() which column is the log2 fold change, the p-value or the FDR. A dictionary shipped with the package (inst/dictionaries/column_patterns.json) holds an ordered list of case-insensitive patterns per concept. The first pattern that matches any column wins, so exact names beat loose substrings:

"effect_log2fc": ["^diff$", "^log2[._ ]?(fold)?[._ ]?(change|ratio|fc)?$",
                  "^logfc$", "^estimate$", "log2"],
"score_pvalue":  ["^p[._ ]?value$"],
"score_fdr":     ["^fdr$", "^adj[._ ]?p[._ ]?val(ue)?$", "^padj$",
                  "^q[._ ]?val(ue)?$", "^p[._ ]?adjusted$", "fdr"],
"score":         ["score"],
"used_in_test":  ["^used[._ ]?in[._ ]?test$"]

This covers DESeq2, edgeR, limma, and prolfqua out of the box. It also covers SAINTexpress, whose tables have log2_EFCs, BFDR, and SaintScore and no p-value at all: log2_EFCs matches log2, BFDR matches fdr, and SaintScore becomes an extra score. That score is shown in the DE table and offered as a volcano y-axis; significance thresholds still use the FDR. With no p-value, the app works from the FDR alone.

The rowdata side works the same way for gene IDs, symbols, descriptions, protein and peptide IDs, phospho sites, and GO columns.

Only the recognised statistics are stored for each contrast, plus a usedInTest flag when the table has one (SUSHI’s expression filter; the DE views then show only the tested features). Without it, a feature counts as tested when its p-value isn’t NA. Other DE-table columns (e.g. a per-contrast avgAbd) are not kept; put per-feature annotation in rowdata, where every column is kept.

When a column isn’t recognised

build_explore_h5ad() warns, naming the contrast, the field it couldn’t fill, and the columns it saw. Two fixes:

  • For one file: name the columns yourself. Five keys exist; anything you don’t name is still found by the dictionary.

    build_explore_h5ad(...,
  de_columns      = list(effect_log2fc = "<your column>",
                         score_pvalue  = "<your column>",
                         score_fdr     = "<your column>"),
  rowdata_columns = list(id_col = "<your column>", symbol_col = "<your column>"))

    de_columns applies to every contrast, or pass a list of such lists named by contrast. The mapping is saved in the file.

  • For a naming convention you’ll see again: add a pattern to inst/dictionaries/column_patterns.json. It’s a JSON edit, not a code change; put anchored patterns (^...$) before loose ones.

Feature level

feature_level is detected from rowdata: a site column means phospho, a peptide_Id column means peptide, and a transcript_id column with one transcript per row means isoform. Otherwise it’s gene (RNA-seq) or protein (proteomics). Pass feature_level = to override.

Organisms without an annotation package

Nothing in the file needs an organism database. Leave organism and ref_build out, and use your own gene ids as the rownames of the counts. What changes is what the app can offer:

  • KEGG tabs appear only for human, mouse, and rat.
  • GO tile plots and the GO heatmap appear when rowdata has GO annotation columns: Any of GO BP, GO MF, and GO CC, each holding "; "-separated GO ids (NA for none). One ontology is enough.
  • ORA / GSEA show the results you pass in pathways; the app never runs enrichment itself.

If your annotation is one list of GO ids per gene (e.g. eggNOG-mapper’s comma-separated GOs column), split it by ontology with GO.db:

# annot: one row per gene, with gene_id and GOs ("GO:0008150,GO:0003674", or "-")
ids  <- strsplit(annot$GOs, ",", fixed = TRUE)
long <- data.frame(gene_id = rep(annot$gene_id, lengths(ids)), go = unlist(ids))
long <- long[grepl("^GO:", long$go), ]
long$ontology <- AnnotationDbi::Ontology(long$go)   # "BP", "MF" or "CC"
for (ont in c("BP", "MF", "CC")) {
  hits     <- long[long$ontology %in% ont, ]
  per_gene <- split(hits$go, factor(hits$gene_id, levels = annot$gene_id))
  annot[[paste("GO", ont)]] <- vapply(per_gene, function(x)
    if (length(x)) paste(x, collapse = "; ") else NA_character_, "")
}

For pathway results, run clusterProfiler’s enricher() (or GSEA()) with a TERM2GENE built from the same annotation. The example below does this on the shipped dataset as if it had no annotation package: It keeps only the GO BP column, builds TERM2GENE from it, and runs ORA on the up-regulated genes against the tested ones. Gene ids in TERM2GENE must be the rownames of your counts.

rd  <- rowData(se)
bp  <- strsplit(as.character(rd[["GO BP"]]), "; ", fixed = TRUE)
t2g <- data.frame(term = unlist(bp), gene = rep(rownames(rd), lengths(bp)))
t2g <- t2g[!is.na(t2g$term), ]

tested <- rownames(rd)[rd$usedInTest]
up     <- rownames(rd)[rd$usedInTest & !is.na(rd$fdr) & rd$fdr < 0.05 & rd$log2Ratio > 0]
ora_up <- clusterProfiler::enricher(up, TERM2GENE = t2g, universe = tested)

build_explore_h5ad(
  x        = list(counts = assay(se, "counts"), normalised = assay(se, "xNorm")),
  out      = file.path(out_dir, "own_annotation.h5ad"),
  omics    = "rnaseq",
  coldata  = colData(se),
  rowdata  = rd[, c("gene_id", "gene_name", "description", "GO BP")],
  factors  = "Condition [Factor]",
  de       = list(diff_vs_undiff = rd),
  pathways = list(diff_vs_undiff = list(ora = list(BP = list(upGenes = ora_up))))
)

Name the nested results as the app shows them: The ontology (BP, MF, CC, or your own label), then the direction (upGenes, downGenes, bothGenes).

Writing the file outside R

If your pipeline isn’t in R (a Python script, an exporter app), write the .h5ad yourself following the format spec that ships with the package:

system.file("spec/exploreDE-h5ad-1.0.md", package = "exploreDE")

It lists every required key, the proteomics profile (protein, peptide, phospho, and precursor levels), and a minimal Python writer that has been checked against the reader. Check the result with new_explore_dataset() as above. APB Export’s exploreDE output and the prolfquapp DEA’s AnnData.h5ad (prolfquapp 2.10.x) open as they are.

Opening a file from a link

On a server, ?data= takes a percent-encoded https:// link to an .h5ad from an allowed source, for example https://shiny-public.fgcz.uzh.ch/app/exploreDE/?data=https%3A%2F%2F...%2Fmy_data.h5ad. The default sources are APB Export jobs and public pStore; set the environment variable EXPLOREDE_URL_SOURCES (comma-separated https:// prefixes) to change them. The file is downloaded without redirects, up to 1 GB, and then checked like an upload.

Saving your settings

The Save / Load Session tab downloads your settings across every tab (widgets, the feature bucket, pathway selections, and Multi DE datasets) as one .json file. Upload it later on the same dataset to pick up where you left off; a session from a different dataset is refused. The file holds no data, and its format is described in system.file("spec/exploreDE-session-2.md", package = "exploreDE").
